Sarah (Customer): Hi team — after rotating our API key last night, several of our scheduled jobs started getting 403s when calling Redwood endpoints in eu-west. Hits started ~02:10 UTC. No other error details from our side, customer-facing error is 403 Forbidden.
Maya (Support): Sorry about that — can you paste one failing request id/header? Also which endpoint and region?
Sarah (Customer): sample request id from logs: req_0a12b34c. Endpoint: https://api.eu-west.redwood.com/v1/generate (text generation). We rotate keys via Vault KV v2 and then update service env.
Tom (Eng): thx. @Maya can you check auth logs for req_0a12b34c and any auth-revocation events around 02:10 UTC?
Maya (Support): Pulling logs now. deploy-bot: auth-check completed for req_0a12b34c -> outcome: denied, upstream reason: key_revoked, auth-actor: service-principal:jobs-runner-eu.
Li (SRE): Quick thought — sometimes sidecars / kube secrets keep old envs until restart. Also Vault path mismatches can leave one consumer pointed at old secret. Can the customer confirm Vault key path used by jobs-runner-eu?
Sarah (Customer): Jobs use path secret/data/projects/alpha/services/jobs-runner (KV v2). But during a rename last month we moved some credentials under secret/data/projects/alpha/services/jobs-runner-eu and I *thought* jobs were switched. I'll check.
Maya (Support): While you check, can you run a curl test from one failing pod with the rotated key and from a different pod after restarting job? That will help isolate stale env vs revoked propagation. Example repro commands: 
```
# from host/pod with current env
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  https://api.eu-west.redwood.com/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
# look for HTTP/1.1 200 or 403 and X-Request-ID header
```
Tom (Eng): Also include this header in logs if possible: X-Redwood-Auth-Info (we emit detailed auth path used).
Sarah (Customer): Ran the curl inside one of the failing pods. Got 403, X-Request-ID: req_0a12b34c, X-Redwood-Auth-Info: kv=v2:path=secret/data/projects/alpha/services/jobs-runner
Maya (Support): That string is the clue — the request is authenticating using the old Vault path (jobs-runner) not jobs-runner-eu. That means the pod's env hasn't been updated despite the new secret being at jobs-runner-eu.
Li (SRE): Two actionable causes: 1) Job pod still has old env var value stored in k8s secret/ConfigMap; 2) Sidecar or injector writes the env from an outdated secret ref. Quick checks: `kubectl get pods -l app=jobs-runner -o yaml` and `kubectl describe pod <pod>` to inspect envFrom.
Sarah (Customer): Confirmed: the failing pods reference k8s secret name jobs-runner-secret (old). The new automation updated Vault but created a new k8s secret jobs-runner-eu-secret and the deployment rollout didn't point at it. I rolled one pod to test and it succeeded (200).
Tom (Eng): Good catch. Can you roll the deployment/daemonset and then rotate+revoke properly? Steps: 1) point deployment to correct secret, 2) restart pods or k8s rollout restart, 3) verify curl returns 200, 4) once all consumers use new key, revoke old key in Vault.
Maya (Support): I'll keep the thread open until all jobs validated. Also recommend adding a short TTL on the old key for safety and an alert that compares Vault path vs k8s secret refs.
Sarah (Customer): Rolling now. Quick question — is there any chance Redwood's edge cache could hold an auth decision that would keep denying even after pods update?
Li (SRE): Not for auth tokens — we evaluate token per request. Edge caches may cache responses but 403s are not cached by default for our API. So once pod env is updated and calls authenticated, you should see success immediately.
Maya (Support): Follow-up checklist I created for you: 
• Verify all pods reference jobs-runner-eu-secret
• rollout restart deployment/jobs-runner (or delete pods)
• test 3 pods across AZs with curl sample above
• when confirmed, mark old key in Vault as disabled, then revoke after 1 hour
• optionally add a CI step to validate k8s secret names match Vault paths

Tom (Eng): For our internal runbook I logged a short snippet to check Vault -> k8s mapping: 
```bash
# list k8s secrets referencing a vault path (grep in Helm templates / automation output)
kubectl get secrets -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}:{.data.VAULT_PATH}\n' | grep jobs-runner
```
Maya (Support): Sarah — any remaining 403s after your roll?
Sarah (Customer): After rolling all 6 pods (eu-west AZs), jobs are green. No 403s for the last 30m. We'll follow your revoke plan in one hour. Thanks everyone! :tada:
Maya (Support): Great — closing once old key is revoked. Please ping if anything resurfaces.
